Q: I get stuck learning HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (I am a student) A:

Your idea of rewriting manually the exercice is a good start, but creating from scratch is also essential. "Learning by doing" is one of the best way to understand and learn, by being confronted to problems and having to solve them.

But, taking a real course, step by step, is, in my option, the most important. You need someone to transfer his knowledge, via a book, an online course, a website, videos, etc. There are a lot of concepts to learn and I think it is quite important to learn them step by step.

I have taught evening courses in HTML and CSS on several occasions to students on work-based training programmes who are looking to change career direction. This is the concepts I decided to present:

  • Some network bases:

    • what is a MAC address.
    • IP address (v4 and v6).
    • DNS queries and hosts file.
    • router, firewall, setting up a home local network.
    • port forwarding.
    • networking tools (ping, traceroute, dig, wget, etc).
    • how HTTP requests work with some command line examples with telnet and curl.
    • what are HTTP headers and how to use them in both queries and responses (for caching, authentication, etc).
    • configuring a web server with multiple virtual hosts and showing how to deploy static websites.

  • HTML:

    • the XML syntax and difference with HTML, which is more forgiving.
    • HTML validation and correction.
    • Install and set up Visual Studio Code with a bunch of useful extensions:
      • HTML CSS Support
      • IntelliSense for CSS class names in HTML
      • CSS Peek
      • ESLint
      • Emmet Live
      • EditorConfig
      • Path Intellisense
      • Prettier - Code formatter
      • SCSS IntelliSense
      • Live Sass Compiler
      • Rewrap
      • SonaQube for IDE
    • all the most important HTML tags to know and what they are for, with some examples and exercices.
    • how to structure your HTML for good semantics (using the correct tags). Have a look at html5doctor.com.
    • how to make your HTML clear for SEO (search engine optimisation), how to add microdata to your page (see schema.org) and add Open Graph tags for sharing your pages in a clean way on social networks.
    • I suggest to dive into web.dev/html.

  • CSS:

    • prohibit inline styling and always separate content and design (checkout https://csszengarden.com to see why).
    • learn all the CSS selectors, with examples.
    • explain how specificity works (weight of the selectors) and train it with examples to override some CSS rules coming from a CSS framework or an existing website.
    • explain the box models, how margins work (different behaviors), padding.
    • positionning (relative, absolute, fixed, sticky, etc)
    • float (for images, mainly, since new CSS features replace it).
    • CSS table vs flexbox vs grid, with simple examples like a webpage header.
    • media queries for print and all devices.
    • using custom web fonts and creating one with icomoon.io.
    • show the power of SASS/SCSS and why to use it instead of plain CSS.
    • finaly use the good CSS features such as custom properties (CSS variables), transitions, animations, and so on. If you can avoid JavaScript, then try to use pure HTML and CSS.
    • A lot of these concepts are nicely explained at web.dev/css.
    • Also check the guides on CSS Tricks.

  • For the JavaScript part, I would suggest first learning all the base concepts of programming (in any language), so that you can undersand what variables, constants, data types and all the controll flow instructions are made for (if, else, switch, loops, etc). Then, learn what JavaScript is made for in a web page:

    • interactive front end behaviors which you can't do with HTML and CSS only.
    • fetching some data without reloading the page (the good old Ajax concepts and now the new Fetch API).
    • saving some user preferences and re-applying them.
    • doing some operations in the visitors browser instead of doing it on your server, to reduce the server load (ex: generate a PDF in JS instead of PHP).
    • again, have a look at web.dev/javascript.

  • Optimisation and security:

    • Minify CSS and JS.
    • compress it with Brotli and/or GZip to reduce bandwidth usage and load time.
    • do this with tools like Vite, esbuild or Parcel.
    • set correct HTTP headers for assets caching.
    • include versions in URLs to force downloading updated assets.
    • set up HTTPS/SSL by bying a certificate or using Let's Encrypt.
    • set correct folder and file permissions on the server, for security reasons.
    • create a static web site with a static website generator like 11ty, Hugo or Jekyll.
    • Explain what are the risks with server-side logic and what is XSS, SQL injection, uploading malware and launching it remotely, CMS updates which are so important, input filtering and validation.

Q: Test reruns on azure pipeline have stopped working A:

Root cause now found.

I forget we have updated MsTest Framework and TestAdaptor from V3.11.1 to V4.3.2.

when we reverted back to 3.11.1 the problem went away, trouble is we are still using depreciated versions so a long term fix is now required.

Q: KrbException: Do not have keys of types listed in default_tkt_enctypes available A:

It's complaining that you used an incompatible algorithm when creating the keytab. When creating the keytab. I usually use RC4-HMAC:

kutil
addent -password -p username@MYDOMAIN.COM -k 1 -e RC4-HMAC
wkt username.keytab
quit

Now it works fine.

Q: sum of column in XML publisher A:

If you have a column by name, (say CASH), you can calculate the sum of the column values simply by using < ? sum(CASH) ? >, without using repeating-group.

Q: feign.RetryableException: Connection reset executing GET A:

A lot of time has passed since the question, but my solution maybe will help someone. I faced java.net.SocketException: Connection reset during calling FeignClient. To fix it i change used OpenJDK to Oracle JDK and exception was gone! So, i really don't know root of the problem, but changing jdk works for me.

Q: WordPress ContactForm7 datepicker field - disable/block specific dates? A:

it can be done by two types

  • set mindate and maxdate
  • when you open the datepicker and change month/year it will fire an event beforeShowDay with each date on that month and year, and you can check for each date in that function with your date range array or object and return true or false. If false return that date will be deactive and on true that date will be active

Check out this link: http://jqueryui.com/demos/datepicker/#inline http://jqueryui.com/demos/datepicker/#min-max

The description says this: "Set the beginning and end dates as actual dates (new Date(2009, 1 - 1, 26)), as a numeric offset from today (-20), or as a string of periods and units ('+1M +10D')"
